title: Salt Lake to Bozeman
placeholder: Placeholder · late May to early October
subtitle: One-way north from Salt Lake City. Timpanogos, Golden Spike and Fossil Butte on Day 1, the pioneer trails, Grand Teton and the Rockefeller Parkway on Day 2, then Old Faithful, Mammoth and out the Roosevelt Arch to Bozeman on Day 3.

days.title: Before the trip
days.meta: No stamps · this trip starts with an early flight
days.html:
✈︎

Fly in Day 1 morning

Take the first wave out of OAK or SFO to SLC and land by about 9:00 AM Mountain. Clocks jump an hour ahead of home. Day 1 only works with an early arrival.

Pick up a one-way rental, SLC → BZN (Costco Travel). Drop fees can add $200–500+, so compare companies.

Fly home from Bozeman on Day 3 any time after about 5:30 PM. BZN has fewer flights on holiday weekends; price that leg first.

Late flight? If you land after about 10:30, drop Timpanogos (it’s 40 minutes the wrong way) and keep Golden Spike and Fossil Butte.
Once dates are set: book Grant Village Lodge (or Old Faithful) first, since it sells out about a year ahead, then the Montpelier hotel. Juneteenth (Jun 18–20, 2027) is the safest window: everything on the route is on summer hours.

days.title: Utah stamps, then Fossil Butte
days.sub: SLC → American Fork Canyon → Promontory → Kemmerer → Montpelier
days.cut: Fossil Butte closes at 5:30 PM in summer, so arrive by about 4:45 at the latest. Lunch is grab-and-go in Brigham City.

days.title: The trails, the Tetons, into Yellowstone
days.sub: Montpelier → Star Valley → Jackson → Jenny Lake → Flagg Ranch → Grant Village
days.cut: The trail center is closed Sundays, so Day 2 should be a Saturday. Flagg Ranch and Grant Village open for the season around Memorial Day; check if you go that weekend.

days.title: Geysers, Mammoth, out to Bozeman
days.sub: Grant Village → Old Faithful → Grand Prismatic → Mammoth → Roosevelt Arch → Bozeman
days.cut: Yellowstone’s interior roads close in winter, so Google Maps can’t route these legs now; the times here are summer estimates. Download offline maps before leaving Grant Village.

stops.via: I-15 south, then UT-92 up American Fork Canyon.
stops.name: Timpanogos Cave NM
stops.place: Visitor center at the canyon floor
stops.addr: Timpanogos Cave Visitor Center, American Fork, UT
stops.hrs: Summer hours about 7 AM – 5:30 PM daily.
stops.ok: Stamp only. The cave tour starts with a steep 1.5-mile climb, so skip it.
stops.about: Three small, highly decorated caves high on the side of Mount Timpanogos, joined by tunnels.

stops.via: Leave about 10:50. I-15 north, then UT-13 and UT-83 to Promontory. Grab lunch to go in Brigham City.
stops.name: Golden Spike NHP
stops.addr: Golden Spike National Historical Park, Promontory, UT
stops.ok: The last-spike site and the replica locomotives are right outside the visitor center.
stops.about: Where the Central Pacific and Union Pacific met on May 10, 1869, finishing the first transcontinental railroad.

stops.via: Leave about 1:45. I-84 and I-80 east through Echo Canyon and Evanston, then US-189 north past Kemmerer.
stops.name: Fossil Butte NM
stops.addr: Fossil Butte National Monument Visitor Center, 864 Chicken Creek Rd, Kemmerer, WY
stops.hrs: Summer, about Memorial Day – Labor Day: daily 8 AM – 5:30 PM.
stops.warn: Closes 5:30 PM. If you’re running behind, skip the Brigham City lunch stop.
stops.ok: Fish, bats and a 13-foot crocodile in the stone, all inside the building.
stops.about: A 50-million-year-old lake bed, one of the richest fossil deposits in the world.

stops.via: Leave about 5:00. US-30 west via Cokeville into Idaho.
stops.name: Montpelier, ID
stops.addr: Best Western Clover Creek Inn, Montpelier, ID
stops.note: Best Western Clover Creek Inn, or whatever’s open. The trail center is a few minutes away for tomorrow morning.

stops.name: Oregon & California Trails
stops.addr: National Oregon/California Trail Center, 320 N 4th St, Montpelier, ID
stops.hrs: Summer Mon–Sat 9 AM – 5 PM, closed Sunday.

also.name: California NHT
also.where: Same desk at the trail center

stops.warn: Partner site, not NPS-run. Call (208) 847-3800 the week before to confirm the stamps are out.
stops.ok: It sits on the old Clover Creek wagon encampment.
stops.about: Two of the overland routes west, sharing the same ruts through southern Idaho before splitting.

stops.via: Leave about 9:45. US-89 north through Star Valley and Alpine, then along the Snake River canyon.
stops.name: Lunch in Jackson

stops.via: US-191 north to Moose, then Teton Park Road.
stops.name: Grand Teton NP
stops.addr: Jenny Lake Visitor Center, Grand Teton National Park
stops.hrs: Daily in summer. Teton Park Road opens to cars around May 1.
stops.ok: The lake and the peaks are right behind the visitor center. New park for the 64.
stops.about: The Teton Range rises 7,000 feet straight off the valley floor, with no foothills in the way.

stops.unit: John D. Rockefeller Jr. Memorial Parkway
stops.via: Leave about 2:00. Past Jackson Lake on US-89/191; Oxbow Bend is a pullout on the way.
stops.name: Rockefeller Parkway
stops.addr: Flagg Ranch Information Station, Moran, WY
stops.hrs: Seasonal, about early June to early September.
stops.warn: Check the opening date on Memorial Day weekend. Colter Bay Visitor Center, on the way, usually carries the same stamp.
stops.about: The 24,000-acre corridor linking Grand Teton and Yellowstone.

stops.via: Leave about 3:20. In the South Entrance, past Lewis Lake. Summer estimate.
stops.name: Yellowstone NP
stops.addr: Grant Village Visitor Center, Yellowstone National Park
stops.ok: Check in at Grant Village Lodge next door. West Thumb Geyser Basin is 5 minutes up the road for an evening boardwalk.
stops.about: The first national park, set aside in 1872, on top of a supervolcano. Grant Village sits on the shore of Yellowstone Lake.

stops.via: West over Craig Pass on the Grand Loop.
stops.name: Old Faithful
stops.addr: Old Faithful Visitor Education Center, Yellowstone National Park
stops.note: Check the next predicted eruption at the visitor center, then find a bench. It goes about every 90 minutes.

stops.via: Leave about 9:45. North to Midway Geyser Basin.
stops.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
stops.addr: Grand Prismatic Spring, Yellowstone National Park
stops.note: The boardwalk is a longer walk than most of these stops.
stops.warn: Skip it if the lot is full.

stops.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
stops.note: Lunch in Mammoth. Elk on the lawns, and the hot spring terraces are visible from the road.

stops.name: Roosevelt Arch
stops.note: Photo stop on the way out of the park. “For the benefit and enjoyment of the people.”

stops.title: Bozeman → home
stops.note: Leave about 1:30. US-89 north through Paradise Valley, then I-90 west. Return the car at BZN; plenty of buffer for a 5:30 PM or later flight.
